The GG's

By: Tarryn Crossman | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
It started off with 5 besties tired of all day-to-day post mom life and wanting to get back to the one thing that made them happy the sea.
Today there are 96 women that meet every Friday morning to boogie board together.
Rules
No under 50’s
No men
And No children

They talk about feeling stuck. Exhausted from the years of doing all the things they had to do as moms and finally finding a space to just be themselves again.
They talk about growing up in the sea and their best childhood memories being in the water, but over the years of obligation they forgot. Forgot the freedom and the thrill of catching a wave. Until now.

They hit the beach like a wave of grey hair and wrinkles, put on their wetsuits and then Julie always – LETS BOOGIE






Further information:
Characters
Julie - she started the group
funny, candid and outspoken

Susan is 53, blind and never boogy boarded before
She talks about learning the language of the sea and finally being able to feel how the water moves when a wave is coming, instead of waiting to hear it break behind her

Riaan - 71
Lost her husband last year and says her time is now
Within the GG's there is no judgement, everyone is there to be Free

All the GG's speak about universal themes like
Freedom, finding happiness, not getting stuck, finding your inner child

Presenter and camera to EL

Script:


VO 1
As the sun rises over East London, a group of boogie boarders slowly make their way to the beach.

There are close to a hundred of them… all women … suited up and ready for a morning session

JULIE
we don't feel old, you know, we feel like you're 20

SUSAN
I never knew how much speed you can reach on a boogie board.

VO 3
These are the grannies taking to the waves at Nahoon Beach… all of them over 50.

FADE TO BLACK

JULIE
The beach was our playground as kids.
We didn't learn to swim in swimming pools in those days because you were at the beach.
Water is healing.
it controls your breathing, it slows the pace down


VO 4
Julie Schroeder spends her days teaching children a love of water, but says she lost her own connection with the ocean somewhere along the way.

JULIE
You get busy
when your kids are little, and you often get caught up in that.
then boogie boarding did take a little bit of a backseat in my life

VO 5
But Last year, Julie was determined to get back into the ocean. Not wanting to do it on her own, she recruited a friend who - in turn - invited others to join.

JULIE
I asked if we should start a group. And she gave me the thumbs up, and the group grew and grew.


VO 6
One became FOUR…. and eventually four turned into nearly 90 women over 50 getting together every Friday to boogie board.

Sometimes we think, well, the only thing we can do when we get older is maybe go to sewing and crocheting and maybe just go to tea with your friends. But people want to do adventurous things, and that's not an age thing; it doesn't stop. so we've created the space. a safe space whether they're 50 or 80,

VO 7
They called themselves the granny grommets and never looked back.

JULIE
Why the granny grommets
Grommets traditionally are beginner surfers or young surfers. So we the opposite end of the scale. we the old surfers or the old boogie boarders.

The rules of engagement are simple: no under 50, no men and no children.

JULIE
our youngest lady I think is 51 or 52, and our oldest ladies, 89


VO 8
Riana Swanepoel is 68, and worked as a teacher for 43 years. Three years ago, she retired but battled to embrace her new life.

RIANA
my husband repeatedly told me, you, Dad, you're not retired. You have to slow down.
I couldn't relax, and I couldn't do anything.

VO 9
Last year, Riana’s husband passed away, and as death often does, she realized how precious time is…
So, she finally took her husband’s advice and started looking for ways to relax into retirement.


RIANA
I scrolled through Facebook, and I saw an article about the granny grommets immediately, I called my friend Susan and I said, we going?
I had to rebuild another life, and I didn't know how I would be, so this is a godsend.
From the first day, I felt I belonged.

VO 10
Riana recruited her best friend and partner in crime, Susan MATTHEE, who committed to a new adventure despite being blind.

SUSAN
I told the other ladies I couldn’t see … that they would have to watch out because I couldn’t watch out for them!


When I was nine, I was classified as legally blind.
I only operate on contrasts … light and movement.

Were you not scared to go into the ocean with a boogie board?
No. I like physical challenges.

I am surrounded by spirited, happy people, and if you’re surrounded by happy people, you are automatically happy yourself.


VO 11
I needed to experience being part of the granny grommets firsthand, so I switched out my Jozi gear for a wetsuit, borrowed a boogie board and hit the waves.
But, despite not meeting the age requirement, I was initiated into the sisterhood.


JULIE
It's just a space where you can just let yourself go. You don't have to worry.
You're living in that moment.
when you're in the water, there's no space to be your head.

VO12
The joy is palpable… Every wave is ridden with laughter and squeals of happiness.

SUSAN
I never knew a boogie board could go that fast! It was so amazing! Sometimes it makes pa-pa-pa! Like you are going over potholes! And we are indeed in the Eastern Cape!

Susan, did you have to get to KNOW the ocean in another way because of your blindness?

You can hear the wave when it breaks, but you actually have to take it before it breaks. I used to always be too late, until I realised that when the water tugs you, the wave is building. Then you can take him.

So you almost had to learn the language of the sea?
we certainly are starting to understand each other!

RIANA
if that wave takes you out onto the beach where you flat
That's the best feeling ever, I promise you.

LOURENSA LINK

VO 13
But this is more than just a wave-riding party; these women have become a community, and the beach their favourite playground


RIANA
Can you imagine a week without granny grandmas?
No, I sometimes mean the weather's not that good. I don't go, and then I'm really miserable afterwards. I missed out, like, with FOMO—fear of missing out on out of the clinic. We've got FOMO.

LINK ABOUT EXPANDING THE TEAMS TO GRAHAMSTOWN ETC

JULIE
A good lesson from the granny grommets is that you can always have fun. You must never pack that away. Don't be scared.
